beats.text: NVIDIA doesn't build its own chips. So what does it actually sell?
It designs them: thousands of tiny cores doing enormous amounts of math at once. Made for games, ideal for AI.
Foundries like TSMC turn silicon wafers into chips, layer by microscopic layer. NVIDIA owns no chip factory. It owns the design.
But the chip is only the start. NVIDIA sells whole systems: networking, racks, entire data centers working as one computer.
And a software layer called CUDA lets developers program all of it. That's why so many AI developers build on NVIDIA.
Who pays? Above all, the big cloud companies, then AI labs and enterprises, all racing for compute. Today, data centers bring in most of NVIDIA's revenue.
So NVIDIA isn't really a chip factory. It designs the engine of the AI era, and sells everything around it.
